headline: Approved lease of School District Office addition at Town Hall and Ordinance 2026-15; motions to reinstate Town Manager Shaun Mulholland failed.
summary: Many residents spoke about the removal of former Town Manager Shaun Mulholland and legal spending. Staff gave updates on High Range Road and other water and sewer projects, and on House Bill 1588 on water special assessment districts. Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard also reported on fiscal management and transparency.
decisions: Motion failed 2-2-0 to seek a second opinion on Town Charter Article 4 from a municipal law firm.
Motion failed 2-2-0 to reinstate Shaun Mulholland as Town Manager.
Approved Ordinance 2026-15, updating Town Charter references in the Municipal Code, 3-0.
Approved scheduling a public hearing on Zoning Ordinance amendments for November 2, 2026, 4-0.
Approved authorizing the Acting Town Manager to enter into the School District Office lease agreement, 4-0.
Council consensus to present the draft Memorandum of Agreement on November 2, 2026.
Approved the consent agenda, including the September 21, 2026 minutes and the October 6, 2026 Timber Tax Warrant, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council seek a second opinion on the Town Charter Article 4 ... Motion failed 2-2-0, with Councilor Bouchard and Councilor Paul voting in favor and Chair Dunn and Councilor Combes voting against.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council reinstate Shaun Mulholland as Town Manager and allow the due process prescribed in the Town Charter ... Motion failed 2-2-0, with Councilor Bouchard and Councilor Paul voting in favor and Chair Dunn and Councilor Combes voting against.

Councilor Combes moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Ordinance 2026-15, updating the references to the Town Charter in the Municipal Code. Seconded by Chair Dunn. ... Motion carried 3-0-0.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedule a public hearing for November 2, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Moose Hill Council Chambers to receive public input and consider proposed amendments to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 4-0-0.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the Acting Town Manager to enter into the School District Office Intermunicipal Lease Agreement and to take all actions necessary to effectuate the agreement. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 4-0-0.
Council consensus was granted to present the draft Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on November 2, 2026.
Councilor Combes moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0.

plain_text:
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 1 
Londonderry Town Council Meeting Minutes  
Monday, October 5, 2026 | 7:00 p.m. 
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Londonderry Town Hall 
Council Members Present: 
Chair Ron Dunn 
Councilor Dan Bouchard 
Councilor Deb Paul 
Councilor Ted Combes 
Council Members Absent: 
Vice Chair Shawn Faber 
 
Meeting Video Link: 
http://173.166.17.35/internetchannel/show/14328?ch
annel=4 
Other Staff Present: 
Acting Town Manager Kim Alan Bernard 
Finance Director Justin Campo 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen 
Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis 
Minutes Prepared By: 
Kirsten Hildonen using Gemini Notebook AI 
 
A. CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Dunn called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance. He requested 
a moment of silence for Lieutenant Michael England of Londonderry Fire, who suffered minor 
burns and a broken leg in the line of duty during a structure fire over the weekend, and for a 
Londonderry High School student who was transported via medical helicopter earlier in the day. 
B. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Michelle Schwartz 
Address: 26 Sheffield Way 
Expressed deep dissatisfaction regarding the removal of Town Manager Shaun Mulholland, legal 
spending exceeding the town budget, hiring multiple law firms without transparent justification, 
anonymous complaints against municipal leadership, and proposed revisions to the Town 
Manager job description lowering qualification requirements.  
Name: Jane Cooper 
Address: 73 Winterwood Drive 
Endorsed Michelle Schwartz's remarks, criticized the exclusion of two Council members from 
executive decision-making and legal investigations, and called for greater transparency and 
kindergarten-level teamwork.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 2 
Name: Resident (Declined to state name) 
Address: Londonderry, NH (Declined to state address) 
Expressed safety concerns, highlighted decades of residency in Londonderry, criticized the 
Council majority for lack of respect toward residents, unauthorized legal expenditures without 
public explanation, and opening the town to potential lawsuits by denying due process. 
Name: Clarissa Navarro 
Address: 2 Woodbine Drive 
Expressed disgust over the complete lack of transparency surrounding the vetting, contract 
approval, and termination of former Town Manager Shaun Mulholland, warned of severe tax 
impacts from potential wrongful termination litigation, and called for voter accountability in 
upcoming local and state elections. 
Name: Brian MacDonald 
Address: 6 Picadilly Circle 
Represented Braver Angels (a national organization working to depolarize communities) and 
requested that the Council finalize three priority dates for holding a "Managing Difficult 
Conversations with Colleagues" workshop. Council discussed proposed dates including October 
26, November 9, or November 23, 2026 at 7:00 p.m.  
Name: Pollyann Winslow 
Address: 4 Hearthstone Drive 
Expressed embarrassment over the sudden dismissal of the Town Manager and the lack of public 
information available, urging Councilors to put community interests first to attract quality 
volunteers and municipal leadership. 
Name: Harry Schwartz 
Address: 26 Sheffield Way 
Addressed the Council on fundamental principles of leadership, fiscal accountability toward 
struggling taxpayers, and the loss of constituent trust resulting from secretive decision-making 
and lack of transparency. 
Name: Martha Smith 
Address: 38 Shasta Drive 
Expressed strong disappointment regarding the Town Manager removal and managing town 
affairs. 
Name: John Romanowski 
Address: 5 Spring Road 
Raised concerns regarding commingled legal bills across municipal departments, requested 
itemized attorney billing by department, and questioned the necessity and million-dollar cost 
implications of terminating the Town Manager for cause. 
Name: Beth Marrocco 
Address: 4 Westwood Drive 
Expressed gratitude to first responders, questioned community safety under dual-hatted 
leadership (Police Chief serving as Acting Town Manager), questioned the legality and process of
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 3 
removing the Town Manager without honoring charter provisions or due process, criticized paying 
$500/hour for non-municipal legal counsel, and urged the Council to stop draining municipal 
reserves. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. Following public comment, Councilor Bouchard addressed 
pressing matters regarding the legal subcommittee formed by Chair Dunn on June 15, 2026, 
unauthorized legal expenditures, the lack of municipal experience among hired legal counsel, and 
the refusal to allow a second legal opinion regarding Town Charter Section 3.02 / Article 4 
interpretations. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council seek a second opinion on the Town 
Charter Article 4 (Administration of Government, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, and 4.5) from one of the 
three law firms that responded to the RFQ with municipal law knowledge and experience 
(Drummond Woodsum or Upton & Hatfield). Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion failed 2-2-0, with 
Councilor Bouchard and Councilor Paul voting in favor and Chair Dunn and Councilor Combes 
voting against. 
Chair Dunn called a 15-minute recess at 7:40 p.m. 
Chair Dunn reconvened the meeting from recess at 7:52 p.m. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council reinstate Shaun Mulholland as 
Town Manager and allow the due process prescribed in the Town Charter and required by the 
courts under the 14th Amendment of the United States Constitution and Cleveland Board of 
Education v. Loudermill. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion failed 2-2-0, with Councilor 
Bouchard and Councilor Paul voting in favor and Chair Dunn and Councilor Combes voting against. 
C. BOARD APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS 
None. 
D. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
1. Receive public input, discuss, and approve updating the Charter references. 
Councilor Bouchard stepped away from the dais. 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen presented Ordinance 2026-15, updating 
numerical cross-references throughout the Municipal Code to align with the revised Town 
Charter taxonomy approved by voters on March 10, 2026, without changing any substantive code 
provisions or procedures. 
Councilor Combes moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Chair Dunn. Motion carried 3-0-
0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Chair Dunn called for public comment. There was none. 
Councilor Combes moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Chair Dunn. Motion carried 3-0-
0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 4 
Councilor Combes moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Ordinance 2026-
15, updating the references to the Town Charter in the Municipal Code. Seconded by Chair Dunn.  
Councilor Paul left the dais at 7:58 p.m., resulting in a lack of quorum. 
Councilor Bouchard returned to the dais at 7:59 p.m., restoring the quorum. 
Motion carried 3-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. Receive a High Range Road water main update. 
Councilor Paul returned to the dais at 8:04 p.m. 
Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis presented a comprehensive update on municipal 
water and sewer projects. High Range Road water main installation is complete to Alexander 
Drive with pressure testing and chlorination underway; paving and striping completed on 
southern sections (Pillsbury to Route 102). Old Derry Road water main is complete and scheduled 
for paving. South Road water main testing is ongoing. The first Saint Gobain water main extension 
into neighborhoods will extend water main along Royal Lane, Imperial Lane, Tyler Drive, and 
Colonial Drive. The Ross/Tokenal Drive EPA-directed superfund water line extension is moving 
forward. On sewer projects, Pillsbury Road pump station wet well construction is starting, 
Bancroft Rd gravity sewer is complete/tested, and Hardy Road force main testing is wrapping up 
with winter shimming scheduled. Addressed property damage restoration along Hardy/South 
Road construction corridors. 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen updated the Council on House Bill 1588 
(effective September 13, 2026), which reformed state law governing Water Special Assessment 
Districts. HB 1588 allows town governing bodies to initiate special assessment districts directly 
with 60% resident assent, eliminating the requirement to track property assessed values. Council 
consensus was granted to present the draft Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on November 2, 
2026. 
Chair Dunn introduced Police Captain Patrick Cheetham, who recapped the 5th Annual Senior 
Resource Expo held Saturday, October 3. The event featured over 70 vendors and approximately 
400 attendees, supported by the Senior Resource Committee, ALERT volunteer team, local 
business sponsors, and founding organizer Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard. Captain Cheetham 
reaffirmed that the Londonderry Police Department stands fully behind Acting Town Manager 
Bernard and assured residents that LPD operations remain seamless under Deputy Chief and 
Captain leadership. 
2. Discuss and schedule a Public Hearing for the proposed Zoning Ordinance 
amendments. 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen presented proposed amendments to the 
Londonderry Zoning Ordinance developed by the Southern New Hampshire Planning Commission 
under a state HOP grant. The amendments respond to 2025 state legislative mandates regarding
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 5 
accessory dwelling units (ADUs), residential parking, and development on Class VI highways and 
private roads, and have received a favorable recommendation from the Planning Board. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedule a public hearing 
for November 2, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Moose Hill Council Chambers to receive public input and 
consider proposed amendments to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance. Seconded by Councilor 
Combes. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
F. OLD BUSINESS 
1. Discuss and approve the inter-municipal agreement between the Town and the 
School District for the lease of the School District Office building addition to the Town 
Hall. 
School Board Chair Bob Slater, Board Member Tim Porter, and Superintendent Dan Black 
presented the long-term intermunicipal lease agreement alongside Acting Town Manager Kim 
Bernard for the School District Office addition at Town Hall. Discussion emphasized 
intergovernmental collaboration, shared maintenance responsibilities, DPW snow removal and 
salting for 70 new parking spaces, and establishing a safe pedestrian walkway for students 
between the High School campus and Town Hall. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the Acting Town 
Manager to enter into the School District Office Intermunicipal Lease Agreement and to take all 
actions necessary to effectuate the agreement. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 4-
0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
G. APPROVAL OF CONSENT ITEMS 
1. Town Council meeting minutes from September 21, 2026 
2. Timber Tax Warrant for October 6, 2026 
Councilor Combes moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by 
Councilor Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 6 
H. OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Liaison Reports 
Councilor Ted Combes reported on the Manchester-Boston Regional Airport 10-year Master Plan 
open house and announced a new direct flight from Manchester to Nashville, TN. Councilor Deb 
Paul reported on Beautify Londonderry roadside cleanups and volunteer road sponsorships. 
Councilor Dan Bouchard commended Leach Library staff for resilient operations out of LPD/Town 
Hall spaces and commended DPW Director Dave Wholley for project management on the School 
District addition 
2. Town Manager Report 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard presented an operational report highlighting fiscal 
management, transparency, and departmental communication. Key updates included restricting 
the Town Council distribution email to councilors only, committing to itemized legal billing in a 
effort to accurately project legal expenses, and recommending the deferral of the police 
department roof replacement project to protect Emergency Maintenance Trust Fund reserves. 
Discussion followed between Councilors Paul, Bouchard, and Acting Town Manager Bernard 
regarding notice of town emergency incidents (firefighter injury/structure fires), solar panel 
rebate incentives associated with roof projects, and advance agenda material delivery. 
I. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Jeff McGraw 
Address: 9 Meetinghouse Drive 
Commended Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen's outstanding support to the 
water subcommittee and highlighted details of the Manchester-Boston Regional Airport Master 
Plan and direct flight service to Nashville. 
Name: Glenn Douglas 
Address: 6 Overlook Drive 
Inquired about the duration and setup of the Council email BCC practice, criticized the lack of 
audio recording during the meeting recess, referenced news reports regarding a  severance offer 
to the former Town Manager, called for a comprehensive legal review of the Town Charter, and 
criticized Council meeting management.  
Name: Megan Donovan 
Address: Leach Library Head of Circulation 
Expressed deep gratitude to town departments  and community volunteers for supporting Leach 
Library operations following the January 27 flood and mold closure, noting thousands of patron 
visits and a highly successful summer reading program.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Page 7 
Name: Beth Marrocco 
Address: 4 Westwood Drive 
Echoed Megan Donovan's praise for library recovery, then urged all Council members to take 
personal ownership of problematic behaviors, refrain from political grandstanding, maintain civil 
municipal governance, and raise standards of leadership. 
Name: Janet Huttula 
Address: 5 Stony Point Drive 
Expressed full confidence in Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard, noted ongoing 
legal/investigative confidentiality requirements, commented on municipal administrative roles, 
and noted town website traffic slowdowns. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
J. NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
None held. 
K. ADJOURNMENT 
Councilor Combes moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 
4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. The meeting adjourned at 9:36 p.m. 
L. MEETING SCHEDULE 
• October 19, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 7:00 p.m. 
• November 2, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 7:00 p.m.
